ECE 6390 / Orbits and look angles

Integration drift

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how different integration methods accumulate numerical error under the same gravitational model.

The physical model supplies derivatives: d(x, y, vₓ, vᵧ)/dt = (vₓ, vᵧ, −μx/r³, −μy/r³). An integrator converts these instantaneous rates into a finite timestep update.

Forward Euler uses one slope per step. RK4 combines four slopes evaluated at trial states, improving the global error from first order to fourth order for sufficiently smooth solutions in the converged regime.

For an unforced two-body orbit, specific energy ε = v²/2 − μ/r and angular momentum are useful diagnostics. A timestep comparison separates numerical drift from genuine changes caused by an added force. RK4 still has finite error.

Example

In the normalized circle μ = r₀ = v₀ = 1, the exact period is 2π and specific energy is −1/2. These provide independent references for a numerical orbit.

    Practice

    1. If an RK4 calculation is in its fourth-order convergence regime, how should halving its timestep change its leading global error?

    The leading error scales as h⁴.

    The leading error should decrease by approximately 2⁴ = 16. A weak or inconsistent change suggests that another error source or a different convergence regime dominates.
